note: PASS with caveat: source paper (Wu et al. 2024, jora.12944) is paywalled and its raw OSF materials (osf.io/jqzbx) contain only the PHQ1/PHQ2 variables with no embedded value labels or item-wording documentation -- the underlying .sav has PHQ1/PHQ2 as unlabeled 0-3 variables. Item text/instructions/response labels were reconstructed using the standard, well-documented PHQ-2 wording (items "Little interest or pleasure in doing things" / "Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless"; 0=Not at all..3=Nearly every day; "Over the last 2 weeks..." instructions), corroborated by a web search summary of the papers own description of using PHQ-2 with a 0-3 scale, but not verified against the papers verbatim Measures section text directly. validate_items.R passes (item/resp sets match exactly).

Item text and 6-point response labels (Strongly disagree...Strongly agree) transcribed directly from the study's own SPSS supplementary data file (s002.sav variable/value labels) rather than the paper body -- the paper's Methods section (p.6) actually mis-describes this instrument as a 5-point scale, which does not match the live 6-category resp data; the SPSS labels resolved the discrepancy and confirm this is Levenson's 24-item Multidimensional Locus of Control (IPC) Scale. No verbatim administration instructions text could be recovered from either the paper or the data file, so the instructions field was left blank.

Forced-choice NPI-13: item_text left blank because the source has no separate question stem per item, only two paired statements (A/B) per item; both statements are instead recorded as option_text for resp=0/1, transcribed verbatim from the study's own SPSS supplementary data file (s004.sav value labels). No verbatim administration instructions text could be recovered from the paper or the data file, so the instructions field was left blank.

Source SPSS file (journal.pone.0259053.s002.sav) stores PADS1-10 raw values as 0-4, but the file's own value-label metadata is keyed to 1-5 (Strongly disagree=1...Strongly agree=5). Mapped resp 0-4 to the same 5 ordered labels shifted by -1 (0=Strongly disagree ... 4=Strongly agree), consistent with the paper's stated 5-point scale and the original PaDS's published 0-4 scoring convention. Validation passes exactly against live resp values; flagging the offset since it wasn't a direct label-to-value read from the file's own metadata.
